Noah Green: opened a small PR to migrate the Ruby SDK snippets in the function-calling guide to the explicit action/args shape and to correct a broken schema anchor. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5061 :mag:
Aisha Karim: thanks Noah. Which files did you touch? I saw a failing snippet job earlier for ruby-snippets.
Noah Green: docs/guides/function-calling.md, docs/snippets/ruby-toolcall.md, and a couple of sample apps. The ruby sample was still using free-form text and the old `invoke` signature. I switched it to show the recommended shape and added an "Advanced: compact envelope" collapsed note.
Ben Rhodes: can you paste the Ruby example you used? Want to make sure it reads idiomatically and passes snippet-ci extraction.
Noah Green: sure, inline minimal example I added (language fence included so snippet extraction works):

```ruby
# minimal Ruby tool call example (explicit action + args)
resp = client.invoke_tool(
  model: "redwood-1",
  input: "Condense the following notes",
  tools: [
    { name: "summarize", args: { max_len: 120 } }
  ]
)
puts resp.body # expected: {"action":"summarize","args":{...}}
```

And I showed the guardrail shape as a JSON literal for readers:```json
{"action": "summarize", "args": {"max_len": 120}}
```

Aisha Karim: nice. Can we add a tiny Ruby fallback helper that demonstrates a balanced-brace extractor instead of a greedy regex? That helped make the docs actionable without shipping a full library.
Noah Green: added a minimal helper under "If the model emits non-JSON":

```ruby
# find first balanced {} region (toy example, not production-grade)
def find_first_json(s)
  depth = 0
  start_idx = nil
  s.each_char.with_index do |ch,i|
    if ch == '{'
      start_idx ||= i
      depth += 1
    elsif ch == '}'
      depth -= 1
      if depth == 0 && start_idx
        return s[start_idx..i]
      end
    end
  end
  nil
end

begin
  parsed = JSON.parse(resp_text)
rescue JSON::ParserError
  candidate = find_first_json(resp_text)
  parsed = candidate ? JSON.parse(candidate) : nil
end
```

Ben Rhodes: good, also add a 1-line Go example to our snippets folder so cross-platform users see the pattern. Keep it tiny.
Noah Green: added a Go example under docs/snippets/go-toolcall.md using the same action/args shape and a short note about parser fallbacks. Example:```go
// Go example (tiny)
resp, _ := client.InvokeTool(ctx, "redwood-1", "Summarize", []Tool{{Name:"summarize", Args: map[string]interface{}{"max_len":120}}})
fmt.Println(string(resp.Body)) // expects JSON shape
```

Aisha Karim: small doc-style nit: replace prescriptive language like "must emit JSON" with softer guidance: "Prefer emitting the structured JSON shape; fallbacks are available when necessary."
Noah Green: updated wording in the PR to the softer phrasing and moved the full JSONSchema into a collapsible block that links to /docs/schema-toolcall.md so we don't duplicate long schema text.
docs-bot: snippet-ci commented on PR #5061  ruby-snippets: 1 failed, go-snippets: 0 failed. See logs: https://ci.redwood-inference.internal/snippet/5061
Ben Rhodes: likely the failing ruby-snippet is missing the language fence in one sample app. I'll take a quick look and push a fix if needed.
Noah Green: thanks. Action items: Ben -> quick patch for any missing fences; Aisha -> skim wording around guardrails; I'll re-run snippet-ci after the fix and merge when green. I'll also add a short checklist at the end of the guide for docs authors: use explicit action/args, include fallback section only in "If non-JSON", link to canonical schema, and run snippet-ci locally before pushing.
Aisha Karim: happy to review. Ping me once CI is green.
Noah Green: will do. cc @docs-bot to trigger docs smoke tests post-merge. :white_check_mark:
